newsitem.title: UK: North Sea Brent crude slips as arbitrage tightens.
newsitem.headline: North Sea Brent crude slips as arbitrage tightens.

text.p: Dated Brent slipped on Tuesday under the weight of ample mid-month cargoes and a narrow arbitrage to the United States but other North Sea crudes were broadly steady despite a deepening contango, traders said.
A Brent cargo due to load June 10-12 moved between traders at July Brent -44 cents a barrel, seven cents weaker than two deals on Monday, traders said.
"There's still plenty of Brent on offer and very little prospect of it moving to the States," said a trader.
A narrow Brent/WTI spread, which lost eight cents on Tuesday to stand at $1.38 barrel was keeping the arbitrage tight.

There was talk of two other Brent cargoes trading but pricing details could not be confirmed. The sole Brent nominated June 18-20 loading dates was kept by Glencore, while a second was deferred to June 23-25 dates, traders said.
Brent paper was also under pressure, July losing 59 cents to $18.93 a barrel by 1757 GMT. Intermonth spreads also gave way with June/July talked at -22/-17 cents and July/August trading at -16 cents.
But despite weakening at the front end of the Brent crude market most other North Sea spot crude seemed to be holding onto their differentials, traders said.
"Regarding the terminal loaded crudes that certainly seems to be correct but on the buoy loaded crudes it seems just a bit weaker," said a trader.

Ekofisk held onto Monday's levels, trading three times in the Dated Brent +17/+19 cents range and UK Forties was even talked a couple of cents firmer amid reports of a trade at Dated Brent +35/+36 cents.

Statfjord, which loads offshore, appeared to be moving in the opposite direction however as a June 23-25 cargo traded at Dated Brent +28 cents but traders put the losses down to softer freight rates. -- Mark Thompson, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7930
